contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-radar-analytics-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-radar-analytics-2026.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-radar-analytics.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics establishes Dashboard fraud analytics navigation to Radar Analytics center and Legacy Radar overview (new raw lines 5-14). It does not freshly describe metric behavior. The May 10 guide describes the newer view as default, with 30 days of history after a 24-hour delay, selection of count or volume, fraud-arrival or payment date, retry deduplication and optional SetupIntents. Fraud, all disputes and blocks are distinct charts. The newer Blocks ratio uses successful payments, while legacy block rate uses attempted payments. Modeled worst-case fraud is conditional and distinct from observed rates (old raw lines 17-48 and 62-102, old raw lines 200-232). The newer Rule matches review outcomes are separate from the legacy Manual reviews panel, which is for Radar for Fraud Teams users and automatically closes a current review if the customer disputes the payment (old raw lines 264-275). Legacy also covers the 3DS/screening/dispute flow, privacy-gated benchmark cohorts, six-month default, exports and daily updates (old raw lines 104-199 and 235-299). source-stripe-radar-analytics.md captures the core views but needs the Sigma access prerequisite, benchmark limits and action/metric distinctions. These are reporting states rather than payment or monitoring program outcomes for a particular account.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/analytics, the November 7, 2026 difference is presentation and navigation: the full May 10 guide had embedded Radar Analytics center and legacy views, and November links the same query routes (new raw lines 9-14, old raw lines 17-23 and 159-165). Neither a product behavior change nor removal of May functionality is evidenced. Preserve the dated 30-day and six-month defaults, 24-hour lag, version-scoped SetupIntent and screened-payment treatment, denominator differences, conditional estimate visibility, similar-business cohort qualifications and continued viewing after opting out, and Sigma permission separate from CSV (old raw lines 30-48 and 62-95, old raw lines 189-232 and 277-299). Preserve the May 10 recurring Billing wording conflict: legacy attempted-payments prose says recurring Stripe Billing payments are not screened (old raw lines 205-207), while the separate Risk evaluations guide says model scoring covers the initial subscription payment and rules evaluate all payments (raw/stripe-radar-risk-evaluation-2026.md lines 38–42). These are source-specific reporting and general scoring/rule statements, and the November selector does not resolve their relationship. Correct source-stripe-radar-analytics.md on the baseline qualifiers without treating them as November changes. Keep both dated raw routes and the existing reciprocal Stripe Radar concept and source links, through the root/provider indexes, and retain the separate dispute measurement and card monitoring routes.
